title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
abstract: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.
